original_question: For an arbitrary permutation class C, determine whether the growth-rate definition gr(C) = lim sup_{n->infinity} |C_n|^(1/n) can always be strengthened by replacing the lim sup with an actual limit.
target_in_paper: The draft matches the open question at the start of Section 7, “Growth rates of permutation classes”: after defining gr(C)=lim sup_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n), the paper asks whether this lim sup can always be replaced by a genuine limit for permutation classes. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
correct_elements: It already captures the core mathematical content very closely: the quantifier is over arbitrary permutation classes C, the formula gr(C)=lim sup_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n) is the right one, and the issue is precisely existence of an actual limit rather than only a lim sup. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Define C_n explicitly as the set of permutations in C of length n. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
State that the paper poses this as an open question immediately after the definition of growth rate. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
Include the nearby special-case context from the same paragraph: the paper notes that this is known for singleton-based classes by Arratia [5]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

Do not add extra restrictions such as finitely based, proper, principal, or singleton-based; the paper asks the question for permutation classes in general. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
refined_question: Let C be a permutation class, meaning a set of permutations closed under taking classical patterns, and let C_n denote the set of permutations in C of length n. Is it true that the sequence |C_n|^(1/n) always converges as n→∞; equivalently, can the definition gr(C):=lim sup_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n) always be strengthened to gr(C)=lim_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n)?
justification: Section 7 is the exact target. The paper first defines permutation classes and their bases, then introduces C_n and the growth-rate formula gr(C)=lim sup_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n), and immediately asks whether the lim sup can be replaced by a limit. The same paragraph gives the only nearby scope-defining special case, namely Arratia’s singleton-based case. The introduction only previews that Section 7 concerns growth rates of permutation classes, so the paper-faithful formulation is this specific open question, not the broader later program of characterizing possible growth rates. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
